clinical_knowledge.topic: Irritable Bowel Syndrome — Diarrhoea Subtype (IBS-D) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Irritable Bowel Syndrome — Diarrhoea Subtype (IBS-D) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Reassurance regarding positive diagnosis of IBS and absence of IBD based on normal calprotectin/bloods, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: crampy abdominal pain and loose bowels for over a year

Key HPI features: 14-month history of lower abdominal cramping that occurs 3-4 days per week, characteristically relieved within 30 minutes after passing loose, watery stools (Bristol stool type 6). Bloating is prominent by late afternoon. Symptoms flare during deadlines at his architectural firm. Denies nocturnal diarrhoea, blood in stool, fever, or weight loss.

Objective/Exam findings: Abdominal exam: mild generalized tenderness without guarding or organomegaly. Baseline bloods: FBC, CRP, coeliac screen (anti-tTg IgA), faecal calprotectin (<50 ug/g confirms absence of mucosal inflammation).
Relevant background/PMH: generalized anxiety disorder, mild childhood eczema
Current medications: sertraline 50mg OD (stable for 2 years)
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Irritable Bowel Syndrome — Diarrhoea Subtype (IBS-D).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Coeliac disease without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: rectal bleeding or nocturnal diarrhoea, unintentional weight loss or anaemia, family history of IBD or colorectal cancer, or onset after age 50.
management_principles: Reassurance regarding positive diagnosis of IBS and absence of IBD based on normal calprotectin/bloods
Dietary modification: reduce caffeine, trial low-FODMAP diet with dietitian
Trial antispasmodic (e.g., mebeverine) or loperamide PRN before stressful meetings
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

learning_objectives: Apply Rome IV diagnostic criteria for Irritable Bowel Syndrome
Systematically screen for and document the absence of red flag symptoms (alarm features)
Explain the gut-brain axis and the role of stress and stimulants in bowel motility
Formulate a positive, empowering management plan avoiding unnecessary invasive testing

teaching.one_liner: A functional gut disorder where stress and certain foods trigger crampy pain that's relieved by passing loose stool, with no structural disease found on testing.
red_flags: Rectal bleeding or nocturnal diarrhoea — atypical for IBS-D and requires evaluation for IBD
Unintentional weight loss or anaemia — suggests an organic cause rather than a functional disorder
Family history of IBD or colorectal cancer, or onset after age 50 — lowers the threshold for colonoscopy

history.answer: I've been dealing with bad stomach cramps and loose, watery bowels for over a year now.
This has been going on for about fourteen months. It happens around three to four days every week.
On bad days I go about three or four times. The stools are loose and watery, never greasy or unusually foul.
No, I have never seen any blood or mucus in my stool.
No, it never wakes me up at night to use the bathroom. It only happens during daytime hours.
The cramping is mostly across my lower belly. It usually eases up within thirty minutes after I have a bowel movement.
I get sudden urges where I have to rush to the bathroom, but I don't feel like stool is stuck afterwards.
Yes, I feel quite bloated and gassy, especially by late afternoon or towards the end of the workday.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, nausea, or vomiting at all.
No dizziness or lightheadedness, my mouth isn't dry, and I'm urinating normally.
I haven't eaten anything spoiled or unusual, and no one who ate with me has gotten sick.
No, I haven't travelled anywhere recently, haven't been camping, and I only drink tap or bottled water.
I haven't taken any antibiotics in years, and I haven't started any new medications recently.
No, my weight has stayed completely steady. I haven't lost any weight.
Cutting out milk or bread didn't really change anything, though having coffee definitely makes the urgency worse.
The cramps and diarrhea flare up badly when work gets hectic, especially around major project deadlines.
I don't get constipated. My gut is either normal or having these loose, watery flare days.
No joint aches, mouth sores, skin rashes, or red eyes.
No heart racing, heat intolerance, sweating, or facial flushing.
I drink about four cups of coffee a day to keep up with my long work hours.
I think my high stress levels at work and all the coffee I drink are messing with my digestion.
My older cousin has Crohn's disease, so I've been worried that I might have something serious like that.
I really want some reassurance and medication to stop these urgent bathroom runs during client meetings.
I have generalized anxiety disorder, and I had mild eczema as a child. No other medical conditions.
I've never had any operations or stayed overnight in a hospital.
I take sertraline 50 milligrams once a day, which I've been on for two years. No over-the-counter pills or supplements.
I don't have any allergies to medicines, foods, or anything else.
I don't smoke cigarettes, but I vape socially when I'm out with friends.
I just have one or two beers on the weekend socially.
I work long hours as a project architect, and I live in an apartment with my partner.
My older cousin has Crohn's disease, but nobody in my family has had colon cancer, celiac disease, or bowel disorders.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, heart rate 74 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, temperature 36.7 degrees Celsius, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
No orthostatic drop in blood pressure or compensatory tachycardia upon standing.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor; sclerae are clear and non-icteric.
Oral mucosa is moist without aphthous ulcers; posterior pharynx is clear.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, smooth, and non-tender without palpable nodules or bruits.
Abdomen is symmetrical and flat without scars, distension, or visible peristalsis.
Bowel sounds are normoactive in all four quadrants; no arterial bruits heard.
Mild generalized tenderness on deep palpation throughout the lower abdomen without guarding or rigidity.
No rebound tenderness in any quadrant.
Liver and spleen are non-palpable below the costal margins; no organomegaly.
Normal sphincter tone with an empty rectal vault; no palpable masses, fissures, or blood on the examining glove.
Normal skin turgor, capillary refill under two seconds, and no rashes or erythema nodosum.
